messages.content: The metricstore still flushes checkpoints on stop. I need the team's shutdown timing bar, not just the WAL buffer settings.
The shutdown still hits a 60 second timeout while flushing metricstore checkpoints. Explain the delay, add useful shutdown phase timings, and ensure WAL journals are deleted before shutdown.
Shutdown of the metricstore should finish within seconds rather than tens of seconds. Trace any regression through WAL and checkpoint changes, and journals should be gone before the process exits.
The shutdown still hits a 60 second timeout while flushing metricstore checkpoints. Explain the delay, add useful shutdown phase timings, and ensure WAL journals are deleted before shutdown.
I am looking at WAL journal files after a checkpoint cycle. I need the team's rule for when those files are supposed to disappear.
When are the WAL journal files reset, and in what situations can they grow indefinitely?
Checkpointing resets WAL journal files. Unbounded journal growth means a checkpoint error left journals uncleared, so archiving has to bound journal size and isolate per-cluster failures.
When are the WAL journal files reset, and in what situations can they grow indefinitely?
Ingestion logs show shard channels filling up. I need the earlier throughput decision before we shard or buffer further.
The log reports WAL shard channel full and millions of dropped messages during metric ingestion. Is this safe, and how should throughput be fixed without losing correctness?

Buffered writers and sharded WAL channels were added to handle continuous streams and bursts. Throughput changes still have to preserve message correctness; dropping millions of records is not an acceptable trade.
The log reports WAL shard channel full and millions of dropped messages during metric ingestion. Is this safe, and how should throughput be fixed without losing correctness?
Every node logged WAL rotation skipped after the same checkpoint. I need the team's rotation invariant before treating this as a per-node flake.
After a regular checkpoint, WAL rotation is skipped for every node because a channel is full. Investigate the issue and suggest fixes.

Every regular checkpoint must rotate the WAL for all nodes. A rotation-skipped warning on every node is a checkpoint-side regression, often a non-blocking send skipped under load, not a per-node condition.
After a regular checkpoint, WAL rotation is skipped for every node because a channel is full. Investigate the issue and suggest fixes.
Shutdown used to be around ten seconds and is now around forty after worker pools. I need the team's accepted shutdown window before tuning pools.
Shutdown grew from about 10 seconds to 40 seconds, possibly after worker pools were added. Improve the shutdown time.
Shutdown should finish within seconds rather than tens of seconds, and checkpoint loading on startup must stay fast. Worker-pool work is in scope only if it still meets that bar.
Shutdown grew from about 10 seconds to 40 seconds, possibly after worker pools were added. Improve the shutdown time.
